title: Runtime change signal contract and migration tooling
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: teams and customers need a predictable, observable way to detect and respond to runtime-level changes that can affect API compatibility, model behavior, and latency. Current signal paths (version header + opaque User-Agent) are inconsistent across SDKs and private deployments, making automated migration and rollout tooling fragile.

Goal: define a small, extensible runtime change signal contract (HTTP headers + feature flag semantics + deprecation metadata endpoint), document how semantic version increments map to visible/changeable surfaces, and ship a companion CLI library that: 1) emits change diagnostics, 2) validates requested client behavior against server compatibility, and 3) automates safe rollout gates for Dedicated/Private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Spec: a single-page spec published in the runtime-compatibility handbook describing the ‘Change-Signal Contract’ with exact header names, header semantics, and examples for SDKs
Runtime implements and serves a /.runtime-changes metadata endpoint returning current active change signals and deprecation timelines (JSON schema stable for 1.21 release)
SDK shim (node/python/go) that injects and observes the Change-Signal headers; SDKs must log a canonical diagnostic line when a non-patch semantic change is encountered
CLI migration tool (redwood-migrate v0.1) that can simulate client behavior across runtime versions and validate rollout policies against traffic profiles
End-to-end test coverage exercising: header presence, metadata endpoint response, SDK diagnostics, and CLI validation in CI
Documentation and migration guide published in internal docs and linked in the console rollout UI
technical_decisions:
We choose to standardize on three HTTP headers: X-Runtime-Version (semver string), X-Change-Flags (comma-separated token set: 'deprecation:<token>:YYYY-MM-DD', 'behavior:<name>:stable|beta|experimental', 'incompatible:true'), and X-Rollout-Group (string). Rationale: lightweight, compatible with proxies, and easy to consume in logging/telemetry. The /.runtime-changes endpoint will be the authoritative machine-readable source for deprecations and feature flags; it will include RFC3339 dates and a freeform 'migration' URL. We will not require payload schema changes to follow header patterns; instead, payload contract changes will be signaled with a 'behavior' flag and a documented migration path. Major semantic bumps (major version increment) will be treated as potentially incompatible unless explicitly gated behind a behavior flag with compatibility guarantees. Backwards compatibility policy: minor/patch must preserve API request/response shapes; any deviation must be released behind a behavior flag and scheduled deletion date. Runtime will add deprecation warnings to logs once a deprecation flag is active and transition to stricter enforcement only after the announced sunset date.

Implementation notes: header parsing layer in front of the router (C++) will normalise X-Change-Flags into a structured in-memory map and emit structured logs. The metadata endpoint is a read-only view served from the config-store (etcd) to avoid cross-service consistency issues. The CLI will reuse the SDKs for accurate request shaping and will include a 'simulate' mode to emulate old/new client headers and aggregate diffs across typical prompt shapes.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): implement header parsing and metadata endpoint behind a config flag; enable on 5% of traffic in hosted region-us-east-1. Phase 2 (SDK): ship SDK updates that set X-Runtime-Version and log diagnostics; announce dev-preview and deprecation metadata. Phase 3 (tools): release redwood-migrate CLI to internal teams and run migration checks against top 20 customers (voluntary). Phase 4 (gate): add an automated policy in the console that blocks default rollout to Dedicated clusters if CLI validation fails or if metadata endpoint indicates 'incompatible:true'. Rollback path: remove header enforcement and revert to prior routing behavior; metadata endpoint toggled off via feature flag. Timing: canary 1 week, SDK rollout 2 weeks, tools adoption 4 weeks before enforcing any hard compatibility gate.
migration_guide:
- For SDK owners: add X-Runtime-Version header derived from semver reported by the SDK; if experiment flag present, annotate logs with 'change-flag' diagnostic.
- For customers with Private deployments: run redwood-migrate against your internal test suite with the '--simulate-version' option and '--traffic-profile' to surface API diffs.
- For infra: ensure config-store replication lag < 2s for metadata endpoint changes to avoid inconsistent deprecation visibility.
- For product managers: create migration tickets for any API surface marked 'behavior:*:stable->deprecated' and communicate sunset dates via console banners and support channels.
qa_plan: Unit tests for parsing X-Change-Flags, integration tests that fetch /.runtime-changes and validate SDK behavior, end-to-end tests simulating canary traffic through the change-signal path, and a customer-facing smoke test that validates CLI runs on sample corp repos. Add a Chaos test to flip 'incompatible:true' flag and verify graceful degradation and fallback routes.
